version.changelog:
**Major update: adds full multi-format build scripts, templates, prompts, and site skeletons for Cookbook-forge automation.**

- Added assets and scripts to support automated conversion from MDX to ElegantBook LaTeX/PDF, Nextra site, and optimized EPUB using both LLM and pure JS pipelines.
- Included full Nextra v3 website skeleton with Dockerfile, config, scripts, and pages for instant deployment.
- Provided LLM prompt templates for MDX→LaTeX and MDX→EPUB conversion, and utility scripts for diagram rendering, formula/image fixes, word count, and font subsetting.
- Added comprehensive style guide references and single-chapter MDX templates for consistent output.
- Updated workflows and documentation to reflect new modular, template-driven, and LLM-enabled architecture.
- Removed deprecated skill-card; all documentation is now in SKILL.md and references.

llm.summary: This book-generation skill is coherent overall, but it needs Review because some conversion and rendering paths can leak diagram content or let untrusted project content influence file writes, shell commands, generated code, or delegated agents.

dimensions.detail: The environment access is partly proportionate to document generation, but automatic Kroki rendering, unsafe shell command construction, unvalidated slug-derived paths, and raw template substitution create avoidable high-impact risks.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No hidden install hook or persistence installer was found. The generated Nextra site does require npm and Docker workflows, with semver dependency ranges and a mutable PlantUML image tag.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The workflow asks agents to ingest many local and remote materials and to delegate chapter conversion via prompt files, but it does not define tight tool or filesystem boundaries for those sub-agents.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No backdoor, scheduled task, or memory persistence was found, but conversion prompt files can retain full source chapter content in plaintext, and unvalidated slugs can write outside intended build directories.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, generating MDX books plus LaTeX/PDF, Nextra, and EPUB outputs, matches the included templates and scripts. Broad file reading, web research, local builds, Docker, and LLM sub-agents are mostly purpose-aligned for this workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable reviewing or constraining the build scripts. Use it on trusted source material, avoid confidential diagrams unless remote rendering is disabled or replaced with local rendering, sandbox Docker/npm/LLM sub-agent runs, and validate chapter slugs and scaffold arguments before building generated outputs.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the Nextra middleware and metadata files are template assets for the documented website output, not evidence of purpose-mismatched behavior.
[AE1] expected: Downgraded: the referenced scripts and assets were present in this workspace and representative files were inspected locally.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted as a Review concern: broad file, network, build, Docker, and sub-agent authority is described, but no tight allowed-tool or path scope is declared.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese defaults and /zh routing are disclosed and consistent with the Chinese-language templates, though users should be aware of the default locale behavior.
[RP1] unexpected: Accepted as a supply-chain concern: the workflow and generated scripts use mutable Docker image tags such as plantuml/plantuml:latest and an image name ending in :latest.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted as a data-handling concern: lmdx2tex.mjs and lbuild-epub.mjs write full MDX content into prompt files for sub-agent conversion, and pending prompt files can remain on disk.
[SDI-2] expected: Downgraded: the Python zipfile subprocess is disclosed and purpose-aligned for EPUB packaging; it is not evidence of hidden execution by itself.
[T01] unexpected: Accepted: the converters interpolate untrusted MDX into prompts consumed by delegated agents without a strong data-versus-instruction boundary.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: frontmatter slug values are used in output paths without validation, allowing traversal outside intended build directories.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: Nextra scaffolding performs raw placeholder replacement into JSON, YAML, and TypeScript/JSX contexts without context-appropriate escaping.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: render-plantuml.mjs builds a shell command using filenames from public/diagrams-src, enabling command injection from crafted filenames.
[other] unexpected: Accepted: diagram-renderer.mjs automatically sends Mermaid or PlantUML diagram source to kroki.io via GET when cached SVGs are absent, despite the documentation framing Kroki as opt-in for confidential content.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted as a caution: generated builds use semver ranges without a committed lockfile and mutable container images, reducing reproducibility and increasing supply-chain exposure.
